title: Corned Beef Sandwich on White Bread

content.title: About
content.content: A corned beef sandwich on white bread is a classic quick snack. Thinly sliced, salt‑cured beef, brined with spices, is placed between two slices of soft white bread. The sandwich is usually served cold, sometimes with mustard or pickles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “corned beef” comes from the English word “corn,” referring to the large salt crystals used in the curing process.
Canned corned beef was first produced on a large scale in Ireland in the 19th century for export to the United States.
The sandwich became popular among sailors and travelers because it stays edible without refrigeration for long periods.
In the US, a classic variation often includes sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Russian dressing – the Reuben sandwich.
White bread used for this sandwich is typically crust‑less to provide a soft texture and easy bite.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Corned beef provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The sandwich offers a quick source of calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Corned beef can contain up to 2 g of salt per 100 g, which may raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: The product contains saturated fats, so individuals with cardiovascular concerns should limit portion size.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to beef or to additives in the brine.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands add nitrites and other preservatives, which can be undesirable in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten cold, cut in half. It can be enhanced with mustard, mayo, pickles, or lettuce. For a softer bite, lightly toast the bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich refrigerated at 0–4 °C and consume within 2‑3 days. Store unopened canned corned beef in a cool, dry place; once opened, keep it in the fridge and use within 5‑7 days.
